div.head: Northu 35
div.ab: Gif preost cwenan forlæte ⁊ oðre nime, anathema sit!
Gif preost cwenan forlæte and oðre nime, anathema sit!
If a priest leaves a woman and takes another, let him be anathema!
If a priest abandons one woman and takes another, let him be accursed!
Wenn ein Priester [seine] Frau verlässt und eine andere nimmt, Anathema sit!
If a priest leaves [his] woman and takes another, let him be anathema!
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.

note.label: contrast
note.quote: Northu. 35; compare (e.g.) VI Atr 5:1-2 ... where it is an aggravation of an already serious offence that priests have more than one wife

div.note: Though marriage of the clergy had to be tolerated, cwene is not a usual term for a legal wife.
This clause’s condemnation of a priest abandoning his wife marks a significant departure from Wulfstan’s thought. For Wulfstan, all clerical marriage was anathema, regardless of circumstance.
